DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 64 s. 2022 JUL 22 2022 Hon. LARISA C. FORONDA Mayor Vintar, Ilocos Norte Dear Hon. Foronda: This pertains to your letter dated 1 3 June 2022 requesting for the Department's opinion on the validity of upholding Municipal Ordinance No. 2020-07. Per your letter, said ordinance was enacted revising the Organizational Structure and Staffing Pattern (OSSP) of the Municipal Government of Vintar, Ilocos Norte, and was declared valid by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan except the appropriations for the newly created position of Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Officer IV (LDRRMO IV) on the ground that it is not in conformity with the provisions of Section 5.3 and 5.6 of NDRRMC-DILG-DBM-CSC JMC No. 2014-1 dated April 4, 2014. We submit that ordinances and resolutions enacted/passed by the Sanggunian enjoy the presumption of validity. By reason thereof, the Department, by virtue of Memorandum Order 2010-02 refrains from rendering opinion and taking actions on presumptively valid acts. Thus, we are not to declare whether Municipal Ordinance No. 2020-07 is valid in whole or in part. Said determination is within the power of the reviewing Sanggunian pursuant to Section 56 of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code" For academic purposes, however, may we address the presumption that the provision declared invalid during the higher Sanggunian's review stands and remains in full force and effect. In DILG Opinion No. 5 s. 2018, the Department settled the distinction between "effectivity" and "validity" of an ordinance. Effectivity is the time by which an ordinance is made effective and can already be implemented and given full force and effect. The same is governed by Section 59 of the Local Government Code. Validity, on the other hand, refers to the substantive requirement of an ordinance, whether the same is consistent with the Constitution and laws which is governed by Section 56 of the Local Government Code. Section 56 (c) of the Local Government Code provides as follows: "If the Sangguniang Panlalawigan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred upon the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang Bayan concerned, it shall declare such "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline Noa: 8876-34-54

ordinance OF resolution invalid in whole or in part. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan shall enter its action in the minutes and shall advise the corresponding city or municipal authorities of the action it has taken. " It follows that for those ordinances/resolutions or provisions thereof declared invalid, the period of which they are considered in full force and effect is from the date of its effectivity until the date of receipt by the concerned Sanggunian of the advice/notice from the reviewing Sanggunian declaring said ordinance/resolution or any part thereof invalid. Upon receipt of such advice/notice of disapproval, in whole or in part, of an ordinance/resolution, any attempt to enforce the same shall be a ground for the suspension or dismissal of the official or employee concerned. On the request to be apprised of the status of the employee appointed to the position declared invalid by the reviewing Sanggunian on the ground of inconformity with the provisions of Section 5.3 and 5.6 of NDRRMC-DILG-DBM-CSC JMC No. 2014-1 dated April 4, 2014, may we recommend that guidance of the Civil Service Commission (CSC) be solicited by the concerned LGU. Incidentally, on matters concerning the establishment of Organizational Structure and Staffing Pattern (OSSP), may we likewise inform you that per information from the Bureau of Local Government Development (BLGD), this Department, the Civil Service Commission is in the process of updating the guidelines based on CSC Memorandum Circular No. 19, s. 1992, and in consideration of Executive Order No. 138 on full devolution. The policy will be cascaded to their respective field offices once approved We hope to have substantially addressed your concerns.
